rationale: Original review abstract names general Parkinson fatigue and lists saffron among several plants. Source-specific full context remains gated.
Existing Isfahan randomized Sargol powder-tablet cohort. Fatigue estimate and date of registration revisions are documented in its study assessment.
Existing CranMood juice trial gives an inconclusive HADS depression comparison. Distinct from COMBAT powder and its planned PHQ-9.
2024 review describes traditional fresh, dried and baked ginger uses including pain; not a controlled grated ginger Parkinson pain outcome.

Thirty-six male nerve-ligated or sham rats received vehicle or supercritical ginger extract for four weeks; von Frey thresholds improved in treated injured animals, but extract, doses and rodent induced neuropathy differ from grated ginger and PD pain.

Andrade 2021 migraine commentary cites three RCTs: feverfew mixture, acute ginger extract plus ketoprofen and prophylactic extract; raw ginger recommendation is extrapolation rather than a raw ginger trial, and pooled mean pain difference combines incompatible scales.
Fresh ginger combined with moxa topically on spine in 90-patient lumbago intervention; VAS and pain scores reported in a multimodal non-PD comparison, without oral ginger or isolated contribution.
Fresh ginger is a food matrix to test pesticide detection; no consumption, patient or pain outcome.

external alcohol-based topical preparation containing fresh ginger alongside borneol, alum, borax and cyperus; gastric-cancer symptom analgesic indication; pain appears intended-use only, no measured result or PD.

IBS-D three-arm trial applies a mixed herbal plaster containing fresh ginger juice to an acupoint, with needling in one arm; abdominal pain reported, topical mixed treatment is not oral grated ginger or PD.
fresh ginger included with white mustard, licorice, earthworm and other herbs in a powdered mixture for arthritis; pain-relief claims, no measured clinical endpoint/result in abstract.
raw ginger added to a dietary porridge recipe for stomach-cold symptoms including pain/vomiting; pain intended use, no patient outcomes or measured pain.

oral tablet blend includes Rhizoma Zingiberis Recens (fresh ginger) extract 400–600 mg plus glucosamine/chondroitin/green tea; claims osteoarthritis anti-inflammatory/analgesic benefit but gives no clinical cohort, pain scale or observed effect. Extracted ginger in complex supplement, not culinary ginger.

fresh ginger is in topical liniment for vitiligo with sesame oil; 100 “clinical trials” patients refer to vitiligo healing, while analgesia claims attach to safflower/Cynanchum properties; no ginger-related pain endpoint. Lexical/indication mismatch.
fresh ginger is a minor ingredient in oral yang-warming multi-herb remedy for cardialgia/chest pain; therapeutic intention only, no measured human pain outcome in abstract.
fresh ginger in oral powdered/dietary mixture for chest/heart pain, palpitation, dyspnea and cough; intended use only, no pain scale, cohort or observed result stated.
raw and dried ginger in wine-soaked topical cloth for cold-aggravated arthralgia/limb pain/numbness; pain claims are intended use, no measured outcomes in abstract.
fresh ginger in complex external coating/liquor for rheumatism, rheumatoid symptoms, disc disease and musculoskeletal aches; intended analgesia only, no results in abstract.

topical ointment includes both dried ginger and fresh ginger among 15 ingredients for wound/bruise swelling and pain. Description claims 1,000 clinical cases with cure/effect rates but gives no design, denominator by indication, pain instrument, comparator or pain-specific result; not usable as measured analgesic evidence.

fresh ginger and chamomile liquid/paste composition (possibly dried ginger); patent metadata labels “analgesic” activity, but claims/description give no pain indication or measured pain result. Broad/use-coded claim only.
fresh ginger-containing fracture ointment/plaster; “less pain” and fracture healing are asserted, with no clinical pain outcome or comparator in abstract.
fresh ginger in seven-herb decoction for heat, pain, inflammation and tranquilization; intended-use claim, no actual pain data in abstract.
fresh ginger among many ingredients in oral formula for middle-jiao cold-type gastralgia; intended-use only, no pain score or human findings in abstract.
fresh ginger optional ingredient in multi-herb oral medication for epigastric pain; pain treatment is indication, not a reported result, with no endpoint data in abstract.
fresh ginger in oral/decoction/pill headache/migraine formula; asserted pain relief, no actual measured clinical outcome in abstract.
fresh ginger slices steeped with many other ingredients into medicinal oral wine; abstract mentions back pain among broad claimed indications, without pain results.
fresh ginger appears in a 48-herb topical composition claimed for pain/skin itching; full patent specifies broad formula and intended indication only, with no human cohort or observed pain data.
fresh ginger juice included in clothing-mounted drug bag for rheumatic neck/shoulder/back pain; utility model describes delivery device and intended relief, no measured pain outcome.

USP safety review describes abdominal pain among adverse-event reports in some turmeric or curcuminoid supplement records. Product heterogeneity and uncontrolled reporting do not estimate a ground-spice Parkinson pain effect.
Manjarix combines ginger and turmeric extracts in rat osteoarthritis. The original abstract reports pain-related changes and provides no isolated plant comparison.

topical psoriasis tincture includes turmeric powder (30–60 g) in a multi-herb/chemical mixture; abstract claims easing pain but no pain outcome, and indication/preparation are topical psoriasis rather than ingested ground turmeric or PD.
The same gated Parkinson herbal review appeared in two expressions. Its abstract provides no ground turmeric pain estimate.
